question: Should crawl-remote deployments adopt the permanent hidden canary rows and fail-closed rollback and release-provenance contract once the stacked ClawSweeper and crawl-remote dependencies land?
rationale: Tests establish internal consistency, but automation cannot decide whether permanent D1 state, older-runtime compatibility, and the cross-repository release sequence are the intended production deployment contract.

options.title: Approve staged landing
options.body: Land the prerequisite query contracts first, run staged deploy-and-rollback proof, and merge this workflow only after observing the exact production contract.

options.title: Use an ephemeral canary
options.body: Revise the design to clean up or isolate canary state so rollback does not depend on a permanent stored-data contract.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Keep the draft open until query-level release provenance and rollback compatibility are independently accepted in crawl-remote.

recommendation.title: Approve staged landing
recommendation.body: Land the prerequisite query contracts first, run staged deploy-and-rollback proof, and merge this workflow only after observing the exact production contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the Gitcrawl deployment stack and can present the intended storage, rollback, and cross-repository landing contract for approval.
